headline: Italy Digital Nomad Visa 2026: Income Requirement, Eligibility and Application
metaDescription: Italy digital nomad visa 2026: ~€28,000/year income requirement, degree or 5 years experience, consulate application, €116 fee and 1-year renewable permit. Full guide.

sections.content:
Italy formally launched its digital nomad visa in 2024, with the implementing decree published in March 2026 and consulates accepting applications from mid-March 2026. It is aimed at remote workers who want to live in Italy while working for employers or clients outside the country.

The headline requirement is income: about 28,000 euros gross per year, roughly 2,333 euros per month, derived from three times the threshold for healthcare-cost exemption. That makes it the lowest income threshold of any European digital nomad visa, well below Spain at around 2,849 euros per month and Portugal at about 3,680. Only active remote-work income counts – passive income from dividends, rents or crypto does not qualify.
sections.title: The 2026 rules and the €28,000 income bar

sections.content:
The visa covers non-EU, non-EEA and non-Swiss citizens in two categories: digital nomads, meaning freelancers or the self-employed with non-Italian clients, and remote workers employed by non-Italian companies. You must be 18 or older with a clean criminal record.

On qualifications you need a university degree, a recognized three-year post-secondary qualification, or at least 5 years of relevant work experience, plus at least 6 months of documented remote-work history. Employees need their employer to confirm no criminal convictions in the past 5 years. The strict rule is that you may not work for Italian employers or clients – remote work only.
sections.title: Who qualifies: nomads vs remote workers

sections.content:
The document list is substantial. You must show comprehensive health insurance with at least 30,000 euros of coverage valid in Italy, plus proof of Italian accommodation such as a registered lease, usually before the visa is issued. Many consulates also expect around 30,000 euros in savings for a single applicant.

You apply at the Italian consulate in your country of legal residence – you cannot shop around for a friendlier consulate. The visa fee is about 116 euros, and processing takes up to 90 days for employees or 120 days for the self-employed. No separate work authorization is required and the visa sits outside immigration quotas.
sections.title: Documents, consulate application and fees

sections.content:
The visa leads to a one-year residence permit, renewable annually for up to 5 years. Within 8 days of arrival you must register with the Questura and apply for the permit, and you can convert to other permit types after 1 to 2 years, with EU long-term residency possible after 5 continuous years.

Family reunification is possible: a spouse and children get co-terminous permits, with extra income required of about 9,900 euros per year for a spouse and 4,950 per child. March 2026 guidance also reported a 50 percent impatriate tax break for qualifying nomads, though you should verify this with a tax advisor before relying on it.
